title: Marcos: PH, US explore ties in technology, superintelligence
summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Wednesday said the Philippines and the United States are looking into a partnership in technology and superintelligence.

blocks.text: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Wednesday said the Philippines and the United States are looking into a partnership in technology and superintelligence.

"Now we are also exploring new areas of cooperation, particularly in technology, where American leadership and innovation continue to lead the way," Marcos said in his speech during the bilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump.
"We also see tremendous opportunities to work more closely through American leadership in superintelligence," he added.
Marcos also expressed confidence that the Philippines and the US will find new and important ways to deepen partnerships.
Meanwhile, Trump described Marcos as his "fantastic" and "great" friend.

"We've known each other for a long time. And I very much appreciate your welcoming me and us back to the Philippines as we reaffirm one of America's oldest and most important alliances in the Pacific," Trump said in his speech.

"With this visit, we're building on these ties to make our partnership even closer, although I don't imagine it can get much closer because of the relationship that we've had for a long time," he added.
Meanwhile, Marcos shared that he ordered his staff to deliver a meal from Jollibee, the country's famous homegrown fast-food chain, to Trump and his delegation "to give a taste of Manila."
Trump arrived at Malacañang on Wednesday as part of his state visit to the Philippines.
He is in the Philippines from November 17-18.

Marking its 80 years of partnership in business, diplomacy, and people-to-people ties, the Philippines and the US launched a new edition of a booklet highlighting the countries' longstanding relationship.

The second edition of the booklet, “The Philippines Matters for America, America Matters for the Philippines,” commemorates eight decades of diplomatic relations between the two countries. —AOL, GMA News
